title: OpenAI-Compatible Free LLM APIs: The Drop-In List (2026)
description: A list of free LLM APIs that work as drop-in OpenAI replacements. Change one base URL and keep your existing code: Groq, Gemini, Mistral and more.
author: freellm.site
content:
Most free LLM APIs are **drop-in OpenAI replacements**: you change the base URL and API key, and your existing OpenAI code keeps working. Most providers in our directory expose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so you can switch to a free provider without rewriting any logic.

That compatibility is the most useful thing to know about free LLM APIs. Code you write once runs everywhere, and switching providers to get around a rate limit, or because a free tier disappeared, is easy.

## What does OpenAI-compatible mean?

An OpenAI-compatible API accepts the same request format as OpenAI's `chat/completions` endpoint, so the official OpenAI SDK works with it once you point `base_url` elsewhere. Your messages, parameters and response parsing stay the same; only the URL, key and model name change.

That's why [switching providers](/blog/openai-compatible-api-guide/) is a one-line edit. You reuse one interface across dozens of free backends instead of learning a new API each time. For more detail, see our full [OpenAI-compatible API guide](/blog/openai-compatible-api-guide/).

## Which free LLM APIs are drop-in OpenAI replacements?

These popular free providers have endpoints that work directly with OpenAI SDK code. Each link goes to the provider's live page with the exact base URL, models and limits.

| Provider | Base URL | Card required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Groq](/providers/groq/) | api.groq.com/openai/v1 | No |
| [Google Gemini](/providers/google_gemini/) | generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/ | No |
| [Mistral AI](/providers/mistral/) | api.mistral.ai/v1 | No |
| [OpenRouter](/providers/openrouter/) | openrouter.ai/api/v1 | No (account only) |
| [SambaNova Cloud](/providers/sambanova/) | api.sambanova.ai/v1 | No (account only) |
| [NVIDIA NIM](/providers/nvidia_nim/) | integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1 | No (phone verification) |
| [Cloudflare Workers AI](/providers/cloudflare/) | api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/ai/v1 | No |
| [Hugging Face](/providers/huggingface/) | router.huggingface.co/v1 | No |
| [Fireworks AI](/providers/fireworks/) | api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1 | No ($1 signup credit) |
| [Cerebras](/providers/cerebras/) | api.cerebras.ai/v1 | Yes ($5 trial credit) |

This is a sample; the [full directory](/) shows compatibility for every provider. Two notes if you're updating older code. Gemini's OpenAI-compatible path ends in `/v1beta/openai/`, not plain `/v1beta`. And several endpoints that used to appear on lists like this are gone: GitHub Models was retired on 2026-07-30, and Together AI and DeepInfra no longer offer a free tier, so code pointing at them needs a new base URL.

## How do you swap OpenAI for a free provider?

Change three things: the `base_url`, the `api_key` and the `model` name. Everything else (your messages array, temperature, streaming, response handling) stays as it was with OpenAI.

```python
from openai import OpenAI

# Before: OpenAI
# client = OpenAI(api_key="sk-...")

# After: free Groq, same code below
client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1",
    api_key="YOUR_GROQ_KEY",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-oss-120b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

Groq's free plan now covers its GPT-OSS and Qwen models (30 RPM / 1,000 requests per day); the older Llama IDs were removed from the free plan in August 2026. To use another provider, change the base URL and pick a model ID from its page, for example `gemini-3.8-flash` on Gemini or `mistral-small-latest` on Mistral.

The same swap works in the OpenAI SDK for any language, and in tools that accept a custom base URL, including [AI coding assistants](/blog/use-free-llm-api-cursor-claude-code/).

## Why does drop-in compatibility matter?

It removes lock-in. Your code speaks one interface, so you can move to the best free tier, get around a [rate limit](/blog/free-llm-api-rate-limits-compared/), or switch to a faster provider whenever you like without touching application logic. A provider outage, or a free tier being withdrawn, becomes a base-URL change instead of an emergency. Side-by-side pages like [OpenRouter vs Groq](/compare/openrouter-vs-groq/) and [Groq vs Google Gemini](/compare/groq-vs-google_gemini/) help you choose a primary and a fallback.

Pick one compatible provider from the [directory](/), get a [free key](/blog/how-to-get-free-llm-api-key-no-credit-card/), and build against the OpenAI SDK. Everything you write will work with every other provider on the list.

faq.q: Are free LLM APIs compatible with the OpenAI SDK?
faq.a: Most are. The majority of providers in our directory expose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so the official OpenAI SDK works by changing only the base URL, key, and model name. Groq, Google Gemini, Mistral, OpenRouter, SambaNova, NVIDIA NIM, and Cloudflare Workers AI all work as drop-in replacements.

faq.q: How do you switch from OpenAI to a free provider?
faq.a: Change three values: the base URL, the API key, and the model name — for example https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 with the model openai/gpt-oss-120b. Your messages array, parameters, streaming, and response handling stay identical. The swap works in any language's OpenAI SDK and in any tool that accepts a custom base URL.

faq.q: Does using an OpenAI-compatible free API lock you in?
faq.a: No, it does the opposite. Because every compatible provider speaks the same interface, your code stays portable and you can move between free tiers with a one-line change. That matters when a free offering ends — GitHub Models was retired in July 2026 — because the fix is a base-URL swap rather than a rewrite.
